children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 9 years old and lives with me here at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a son, Alex, who is 9 years old and lives with you.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you look after him and contribute to the costs of raising him (such as food, clothing, housing, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex - I look after him every day and pay for everything he needs like his food, clothes, school things, and of course he lives here with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming. Now I need to ask about your residency status:

**Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have the right to reside in the UK (for example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, indefinite leave to remain, or another immigration status that gives you the right to live here)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I have the right to reside here. We're based here in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training? I know he's 9, so he's likely in school, but I just need to confirm this.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in primary school - just doing his regular schooling like any 9-year-old would be.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just one final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else also responsible for him (for example, does he live with another parent or guardian who might also be claiming)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me - he lives with me full-time and I'm the one looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:
- Alex is 9 years old (under 16), so he qualifies as a child for Child Benefit
- You are responsible for Alex - you look after him and pay for his needs
- Alex lives with you full-time
- You live in the UK and have the right to reside here
- Alex is in full-time education (primary school)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You meet all the requirements for Child Benefit. You can make a claim through HMRC. Child Benefit is currently paid at a weekly rate for each child you're responsible for.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
